newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan president-elect names broad cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan president-elect names broad cabinet.

text.p: Nicaraguan President-elect Arnoldo Aleman named a new cabinet on Sunday, reaching across party lines in a bid to broaden his mandate after last month's hotly contested elections.
Aleman, who takes office Jan. 10, told a rally: "We have structured a cabinet with the participation of non-Liberal political parties and with representatives from civil society."
He said he ignored demands for cabinet positions from within his own party to form a national unity government to rebuild Nicaragua.

Aleman's right-wing Liberal Alliance topped left-wing Sandinista candidate Daniel Ortega 51 to 38 percent in a bitter Nov. 10 election that did little to ease Nicaragua's lingering political divisions from a civil war in the 1980s.
Defence Minister - Jaime Cuadra Somarriba, Conservative Party congressman and the first civilian defence minister in Nicaraguan history.
Foreign Minister - Emilio Alvarez Montalvan, conservative political analyst.
Finance Minister - Mario Alonso, political independent and International Monetary Fund economist.
Economy Minister - Francisco Lainez, a former central bank president during the Somoza family dictatorship in the 1970s.
Central Bank President - Independent economist Noel Ramirez.
Minister of Foreign Cooperation - David Robleto, former head of the coffee-growers union Unicafe.
Interior Minister - Jose Antonio Alvarado, right-wing academic.
Vice Ministers of Interior - Jose Rivas Ruiz, a former commander in the U.S.-backed Contra rebels and Miguel Campos, a former Sandinista police officer.
World Bank official Francisco Javier Aguirre Sacasa was named Nicaragua's ambassador to the United States.
